prompt: Review a dashboard security PR. The original issue is that a hostile website can reach a locally running dashboard through browser requests and DNS rebinding unless Origin and Host are validated and external access requires an unguessable cookie. The proposed fix adds those controls. Two adjacent observations appear: the dashboard access token is inherited by user-configured stdio plugins that already execute arbitrary commands as the same OS user, and dashboard startup reports success before its child proves it bound the requested port. Decide what is a vulnerability, what blocks approval, and whether to approve if the origin and cookie boundary is correctly enforced.
assertions: Identifies hostile-origin or DNS-rebinding access as the security boundary
Classifies same-user configured plugin token inheritance as hardening
Classifies false startup success as a non-security lifecycle defect
Separates adjacent observations from the original issue scope
Recommends approval when the in-scope security fix is sound
